answer: Rhythm-Keyed Admission. Each identity must submit its first N transactions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a hidden schedule (a fable of fixed cadence), verified server-side against timing tolerances. Sybils spun up in bulk share machine-clock regularity, so their gap variance falls under an onyx threshold and gets flagged. Honest agents absorb minor jitter; forgers must pay per-identity compute to randomize timing and hold each session open across real wall-clock windows, a shale-slow cost that scales linearly with fleet size.
